claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for?** If yes, could you tell me:
- How many children?
- Their ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here in the UK. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your son Alex, who is 8 years old and lives with you in the UK.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions:

**Are you responsible for Alex's day-to-day care?** In other words, are you the one looking after him - providing for his food, clothes, and general upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am responsible for his day-to-day care. I look after him - I provide his food, clothes, and everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great. Now I need to understand your residency status:

**Do you live in the UK?** And if so, do you have the right to reside in the UK (for example, are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, pre-settled status, or another immigration status)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and I have the right to reside here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just a few more questions to ensure I have all the information:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** For example, his other parent or another relative?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. And just to confirm a couple more details:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation arranged by the local council?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he has been in care, but he comes home to stay with me on weekends and during the week as well - he spends quite a bit of time at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that. This is an important detail. Let me ask for more specifics:

**How much time does Alex spend at home with you each week?** For example:
- Does he spend at least 24 hours per week at home with you?
- Or does he spend 2 nights in a row each week at home, or 7 days or more in a row at home?

Also, **how long has Alex been in care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, he spends at least 24 hours a week at home with me - he's home on weekends and some evenings during the week.

As for how long he's been in care, it's been about 3 months now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing those details. That's very helpful.

Just one final question to complete my assessment:

**Is the local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance while he's in care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying me anything for his accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Good News!

**You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

Although Alex has been in care for about 3 months (which is longer than the usual 8-week limit), you qualify under an important **exception to the rule**. Child Benefit can continue for children in care when they spend **at least 24 hours per week at home** with you - and Alex does this through his weekend and evening visits.

You also meet all the other standard eligibility requirements:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK and have the right to reside here
- You're responsible for Alex's day-to-day care
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- The local council isn't paying you for his accommodation or maintenance

You should be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex. If you haven't already claimed, you can apply online or by post. If you have any questions about your specific situation, you can contact the Child Benefit Office for further guidance.
